facts.fact: The Department of Home Affairs states that information from Notice of Birth (DHA-24) forms is used to capture births onto the National Population Register at local offices and health facilities; birth and death registration are both listed as front-office services, but no digital capture of deaths is described (undated in the plan; dated to its tabling, September 2025).

The Department of Home Affairs states that births are captured onto the National Population Register at local offices and health facilities from the paper Notice of Birth (DHA-24) form, with the original forms archived for verification and online applications to follow once e-Birth is introduced (undated in the plan; dated to its tabling, September 2025).

The Department of Home Affairs defines its online birth registration system as a service point in a health facility that processes birth registration applications, verifies and authenticates clients online on the spot and issues the birth certificate before the child leaves (undated in the plan; dated to its tabling, September 2025).

The Department of Home Affairs states that as at 31 March 2024 it rendered services at 391 health facilities where it had established a presence and equipped them with birth registration systems, alongside 323 front offices and 220 mobile offices; it gives no count of the offices that capture births digitally and no total of health facilities.
facts.system: birth registration systems at health facilities

facts.fact: The Department of Home Affairs' own annual performance plan for 2025/26 sets the targets for the online birth registration system and for automated birth functionality, with its Deputy Director-General: Operations responsible for the online birth registration indicator.

The Department of Home Affairs' amended annual performance plan for 2025/26 names the online birth registration system and targets its rollout in 9 health facilities with maternity wards in the year (4 in the third quarter, 5 in the fourth), a list cut from 25, after 8 in 2023/24 and 48 in 2024/25.

The Department of Home Affairs' amended annual performance plan for 2025/26 targets automated birth functionality (e-Birth) for first registrations and births to foreign nationals at 47 named health facilities by the fourth quarter, with the legacy system to run in parallel for a year and then be discontinued.

The Department of Home Affairs' annual performance plan for 2025/26 shows, as its district development annexure reads, a budget allocation of R21 million against the rollout of the online birth registration system (issuing birth certificates on the spot at health facilities).

note: Passages only, from a plan tabled September 2025 (the URL carries 3 Nov 25). The 391 health facilities with birth registration systems (31 March 2024) and the online birth registration rollout counts (8, 48, 9) are given separately and not reconciled by the plan. Also stated: 220 mobile offices serve rural and remote areas; target of 667,000 births registered within 30 days in 2025/26, cut because Home Affairs works weekday hours only and not all health facilities have permanent staff; automation of late registration of birth is listed as a risk mitigation.
